note: A demo week for an advanced singer: three practice days of about 27 minutes, built to show many tools in a short week. The hard leaps are the key skill and return on all three days: the tritone and the minor 6th found from Sol, both 7ths found from the high Do and then read inside tunes, and all of them with the voice hidden. Around them sit breathwork, a lip roll and the vowel guide, fast runs, a song chart with its chords hidden, and guide-tone lines over a ii-V-I.

plan.title: Week 1: hard leaps, fast runs and lines that follow the chords
plan.summary: Three practice days of about 27 minutes. Day 1 finds the tritone and the minor 6th from Sol, then sings guide tones over a ii-V-I. Day 2 takes five vowels across the break and sings both 7ths, alone and in tunes read from the staff. Day 3 names the chords of a song with the chart hidden, sings the hard leaps without seeing your voice and ends with a line that leaps wide.
plan.progress:
Breath & range: in, hold and out up to 11 counts; a hiss then a buzz, held for longer; a lip roll, then five vowels on the notes between the two breaks. Next: counts up to 12.
Intervals & leaps: sings the tritone and the minor 6th found from Sol, and both 7ths found from the high Do; the hard leaps with the voice not drawn. Next: the hard leaps down from Do.
Runs: a fast pentatonic run and the octave run. Next: a run past the octave.
Melodies: read tunes with a 7th from the staff. Next: tunes with an octave.
Harmony & improvising: guide tones over a ii-V-I, and a line of guide tones with a wide leap. Next: guide tones round a turnaround.
Ear: hears the tritone and the minor 6th around the 5th, tells 6ths, 7ths and the octave apart, names the chords of a song with the chart hidden. Next: the hard leaps falling.

days.theme: Vowels across the break, and the 7ths
Chords by ear, and leaps you can't see
